q: The nurse is caring for a 75-year-old client who has just been diagnosed with cancer. The client’s spouse has requested that the client not be told of the diagnosis because it would be devastating to the client. The client asks the nurse if the diagnosis is cancer. Which of the responses by the nurse reflects the ethical principle of veracity?
o: “Let me contact your health care provider (HCP) to talk to you about your diagnosis.”
“Any serious health care issues will be discussed with you and your family before you are discharged.”
“At this time, I do not know your diagnosis because the tests were inconclusive.”
“Your doctor is the only one who can discuss health care issues with you.”

key.why: The nurse should practice veracity by ensuring the client receives truthful information and arranging for the provider to discuss the diagnosis.

q: The nurse has attended a conference on informed consent. It indicates a correct understanding of the conference if the nurse states that informed consent:
o: Is signed by the nurse to indicate that the client understands the procedure.
May not be withdrawn by the client once they have confirmed understanding and signed the consent.
Can be signed by a client who has dementia if they are oriented at the time of signing the form.
Can be waived, per facility policy, for urgent medical or surgical treatment if the client is unconscious.

key.why: Informed consent may be waived for urgent treatment if the patient is unconscious and immediate intervention is needed.

q: The nurse is prioritizing client care after receiving the hand-off report. The nurse should first plan to see the client who:
o: Has cirrhosis, reports several new areas of ecchymosis, and has a partial thromboplastin time (PTT) of 76 seconds.
Has pancreatitis and is reporting mid-epigastric discomfort.
Had a transesophageal echocardiogram (TEE) 2 hours ago, has a blood pressure (BP) of 106/61 mm Hg, and reports a sore throat.
Had a laparoscopic cholecystectomy 18 hours ago and is reporting bilateral shoulder pain.

key.why: A new onset of ecchymosis and elevated PTT suggests risk for bleeding and requires immediate assessment.

q: The nurse is caring for the following assigned clients who are 24 hours postoperative. The nurse performed a change-of-shift assessment 4 hours ago. Which of the following changes in client condition should the nurse identify as a priority?
o: The client whose blood pressure (BP) was 138/86 and is now 136/84 mm Hg.
The client whose wound drainage was sanguineous and is now serosanguineous.
The client who reports an increased pain level of 8 on a scale of 0 to 10 after receiving opioid analgesic.
The client who received NPH insulin and has a current capillary blood glucose of 110 mg/dL.

key.why: An increase in pain despite analgesic administration indicates a possible complication and requires priority assessment.

q: The nurse preceptor is teaching a newly hired nurse about legal principles when providing client care. Which of the following situations should the nurse preceptor use as an example of malpractice?
o: A client who is alert and oriented makes an informed decision to leave the hospital against medical advice (AMA). The nurse applies restraints to the client to prevent the client from leaving.
A client who is competent refuses an antidepressant medication. The nurse dissolves the medication in food and administers it to the client without the client’s knowledge.
A nurse is plugging in an IV pump that is alarming with a low battery. The nurse notices the outlet cover in a client’s room is loose and proceeds with plugging in the IV pump.
A nurse finds a client who is on a low-sodium diet eating salted potato chips. The nurse tells the client that wrist restraints will be applied if the client does not stop eating the chips.

key.why: Administering medication without the client’s knowledge violates patient autonomy and is an example of malpractice.

q: The nurse is caring for assigned clients. It is a priority for the nurse to follow up with a client who:
o: Is receiving hydrocortisone and has a blood glucose level of 135 mg/dL.
Has multiple sclerosis (MS), reports feeling tired, and is experiencing diplopia.
Is receiving pyridostigmine and reports nausea and congested cough.
Has active pulmonary tuberculosis (TB), hemoptysis, and weight loss.

key.why: Hemoptysis and weight loss in TB are urgent concerns that could indicate worsening disease and respiratory compromise.

q: The nurse working on a pediatric cardiac unit is reviewing the telemetry monitors for assigned clients. Which of the following clients should the nurse initially plan to assess?
o: A 15-year-old adolescent who is reading and has a pulse (P) of 60
A 5-year-old child who is watching television and has a pulse (P) of 78.
A 2-year-old who is playing with toys and has a pulse (P) of 100.
A 1-month-old infant who is sleeping and has a pulse (P) of 180.

key.why: A pulse of 180 in a sleeping infant is tachycardia and needs prompt assessment.

q: The nurse working on a pediatric unit is caring for the following children who have been admitted within the past 12 hours. It is a priority for the nurse to initiate an interdisciplinary conference for the child who is:
o: 4 years old, was recently diagnosed with Kawasaki disease, and recently starting on immunoglobulin therapy.
5 years old, was diagnosed with cystic fibrosis (CF) at birth, and has been hospitalized 4 times in the past 2 months.
8 years old, was admitted with multiple compound fractures, and recently placed in Buck’s traction
3 years old, was admitted with epiglottis, and is currently having difficulty breathing.

key.why: DiGiculty breathing in a child with epiglottitis is a medical emergency and requires immediate interdisciplinary management.

q: The nurse is reviewing the plan of care on a client who is diagnosed with pericarditis and has been in the hospital for 24 hours. The nurse notes that the client’s current white blood cell (WBC) count is 13,000 mm3 and they have a fever of 100.8 F orally. Which of the following actions is most appropriate for the nurse to take?
o: Change the client’s goal to reflect their current status.
Update the nursing interventions as needed.
Notify the charge nurse that the plan of care is outdated.
Obtain an order for an infectious disease referral.

key.why: The nurse should update interventions to reflect the client’s current status of infection (elevated WBC and fever).

q: The charge nurse is reviewing clients’ electronic medical records (EMRs). Which of the following notes by a staff nurse indicates correct documentation?
o: “Dressing change performed to coccyx wound with no adverse effects noted by the client. Client transferred to chair.”
“IV catheter site in left antecubital space is red and warm to touch. IV catheter removed intact. 20-gauge catheter placed in right forearm.”
“Reports of pain in abdomen with vomiting noted. Medications administered.”
“Found client sitting on floor. All 4 side rails were in upright position. Client reports no pain. No abrasions or bleeding noted. PHCP notified. Incident report completed.”

key.why: Accurate documentation includes describing the IV site status and actions taken.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who has brought in their own continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) machine for use while hospitalized. Which of the following actions is most important for the nurse to take?
o: Review the instruction booklet on how to operate the machine.
Have the machine inspected by the facility’s engineering department.
Explain to the client that the hospital has to supply the CPAP machine.
Ask the client when they last cleaned the CPAP machine.

key.why: Any personal medical equipment must be inspected by hospital engineering to ensure safety and compliance.

q: The nurse working on a medical-surgical unit is caring for the following assigned clients when the facility’s emergency response plan is activated. Which client should the nurse recommend for discharge?
o: The client who has chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), is receiving IV steroid therapy, and has an oxygen saturation (SAO2) level of 86% on room air.
The client who has a deep vein thrombosis (DVT), is receiving warfarin, and has a prothrombin time (PT) of 28 seconds.
The client who has suspected appendicitis, intense pain at McBurney’s point, and now reports cessation of pain.
The client who is positive for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), has a nonproductive cough, and a 24-hour Mantoux test reading of 6 mm induration.

key.why: The client with HIV and minor PPD reaction is stable and can be discharged to free up hospital resources during an emergency.

q: The nurse is observing a newly hired unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP) care for assigned clients. It indicates correct client care if the newly hired UAP is observed:
o: Placing dedicated equipment in the room of a client who has herpes zoster.
Wearing a gown when entering the room of a client who has influenza.
Donning sterile gloves to empty a urinary drainage device.
Removing protective eyewear before removing gloves.

key.why: Dedicated equipment prevents transmission of infection in clients with herpes zoster (shingles).

q: The nurse is teaching a class on child car passenger safety to a group of parents. Which of the following statements by a parent indicates a need for further teaching?
o: “The care seat harness chest clip should be at the level of the infant’s armpits.”
“When using a booster seat, the lap belt should be across the child’s upper thighs.”
“Car seats should be rear-facing in the back seat around ages 2 to 4 years.”
“One hand should fit between the infant and the car seat harness.”

key.why: The car seat harness should be snug, allowing no more than one finger width, not one hand.

q: The nurse working on a pediatric unit is reviewing newly written orders for assigned clients. It requires follow-up by the nurse if the primary health care provider (PHCP) orders:
o: Chelation therapy for an 8-year-old child who has lead poisoning.
Discontinuation of hydrocortisone IV for a 10-year-old who has adrenocortical insufficiency.
A fluid bolus of 500 mL over 1 hour for a 12-year-old child who has sickle cell crisis.
A low-sodium client for a 14-year-old child who has acute glomerulonephritis.

key.why: A fluid bolus of 500 mL over 1 hour is too large and rapid for a child with sickle cell crisis and risks worsening complications.

q: The nurse is reviewing orders for the following assigned clients. The nurse should clarify the order for the client who:
o: Presented with clinical manifestations of an ischemic stroke that started 2 hours ago and is to receive IV alteplase.
Had a permanent pacemaker inserted 6 months ago and is scheduled for a radiograph (x-ray) of the chest.
Is diagnosed with acute kidney injury (AKI) and is to receive a low-sodium, low-potassium diet.
Has a diagnosis of polycythemia vera and is to receive 1 unit of packed red blood cells (RBCs).

key.why: Patients with polycythemia vera have increased blood volume and viscosity; giving packed RBCs is inappropriate and should be clarified.

q: The nurse is assessing a client whose labor is being supplemented with oxytocin IV. The nurse should discontinue the oxytocin if the client develops which of the following assessment findings?
o: Dark, red streaks in her bloody show.
Intermittent back pain with each contraction.
Uterine relaxation between contractions.
Fetal heart rate (FHR) of 68 for 90 seconds.

key.why: A prolonged fetal heart rate of 68 bpm indicates severe fetal distress and requires immediate discontinuation of oxytocin.

key.why: immediate harm.

q: The nurse is talking with a newly hired nurse about peritoneal dialysis (PD) and how to recognize peritonitis. Which signs and symptoms from the box below should the nurse include in the discussion? 1. Hypoactive bowel sounds. 2. Rebound abdominal tenderness. 3. Amber-colored urine. 4. Nausea and vomiting. 5. Cloudy or opaque outflow. 6. Diarrhea. 7. Bradycardia.

key.why: Peritonitis symptoms include hypoactive bowel sounds, rebound tenderness, nausea/vomiting, and cloudy peritoneal outflow. Diarrhea and bradycardia are not hallmark symptoms.

q: The nurse is assessing a client who is suspected of having a retinal detachment of the left eye. Which of the following client statements is consistent with this diagnosis?
o: “I see floating dark spots in my left eye.”
“I feel as if a curtain has been pulled down over my right eye.”
“I am experiencing a sharp pain in my eye.”
“I have lost the central part of my vision.”

key.why: Retinal detachment typically presents with floaters and flashes of light, sometimes described as a curtain over vision, but floaters are the earliest clue.

q: The nurse has an order to remove intermittent sutures from a client’s abdominal wound. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
o: Cut the suture by lifting it with forceps and cutting as close as possible to the skin.
Apply adhesive strips to each suture area after each suture has been removed.
Place the removed sutures in a sterile cup and send to the laboratory for culture and sensitivity (C&S).
Remove each suture in order starting at the top and moving toward the bottom of the suture line.

key.why: Cutting close to the skin avoids pulling contaminated suture material through the underlying tissue and reduces infection risk.

q: The nurse is reviewing the morning laboratory values for a client who has a pulmonary embolism (PE) and is receiving heparin. Which of the following laboratory values requires immediate attention by the nurse?
o: Hemoglobin (Hbg) of 10.8 g/dL.
Platelet count of 100,000 mm3.
Activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) of 60 seconds.
Prothrombin time (PT) of 12 seconds.

key.why: A platelet count this low suggests potential heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT), a critical complication requiring immediate action.

q: The nurse working in the emergency department (ED) is caring for a client who sustained deep partial-thickness burns to the lower torso, both forearms, and thighs from a hot grease spill in the kitchen. Which of the following actions is a priority for the nurse to take?
o: Maintain a warm environment.
Inserting an indwelling urethral catheter.
Preparing to intubate the client.
Inspecting for signs of inhalation injuries.

key.why: Inhalation injury is a life-threatening complication with burns involving the torso or face and must be ruled out early. Airway compromise is always priority in burn care.
